about.title: Personal Injury Help in Highland, California
about.longDescription: Highland sees its share of everyday traffic — and with that comes real consequences. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 154 injury collisions, 241 people hurt, and 6 traffic deaths. Corridors like Baseline Street, Victoria Avenue, SR-210, and 9th Street carry heavy volume, and public records show crashes tend to cluster on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. Those numbers aren't a verdict on any road — they're simply a reflection of how much traffic moves through a growing community of nearly 55,000 people. If you or someone you love has been injured here, whether in a vehicle collision, a slip and fall, or another accident, it helps to understand your options quickly. We offer a free case review — we're here to listen to the details and explain what California law means for your situation. Our team handles personal injury claims on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.title: Time Limits Apply
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Acting sooner helps preserve your options.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Perfect
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Certain Damages
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, which can matter for serious injuries.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a recovery. There's no fee to speak with us about your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim. If your claim involves a government agency, the window can be much shorter, sometimes as little as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Highland?
items.answer: Public records show corridors like Baseline Street, Victoria Avenue, SR-210, and 9th Street carry the highest collision counts in the city, with activity often clustering on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a statement about any particular road being unsafe.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront?
items.answer: No. Our case review is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only collect a fee if you receive a settlement or award.

items.answer: We review your situation directly and explain what California law means for your case. We handle personal injury claims and work on a contingency basis — no upfront cost to you.
